biography: Known as Katie, she was an artist and illustrator, daughter of the Rev. [[person:769]Charles Alexander Johns]. She was a Gosling as Kittiwake in 1864-5. She married in 1873 the Rev. John Henry Lloyd, curate of Wormleighton and subsequently Vicar of Fotheringay. He was curate to the Rev. William Harrison, Vicar of Wormleighton, who was married to Mary Kingsley (1852-1931), daughter of Charles Kingsley and a friend of Katie Johns. Both marriages seem to have come to grief. In 1891 she was living apart from her husband and was matron of Annie Besant’s Women’s Home at 193 Bow Road, a kind of club for girls in the East End, with a few resident matchmakers. A.H.Nethercot The First Five Lives of Annie Besant (Chicago, U of C P 1960) 337, calls her ‘Mrs Kitty Lloyd’ and describes her as ‘a devoted Theosophist’. Later her health broke down and she was sent to Ceylon and then to Benares, where she ended her days as the much-loved Matron of the Central Hindu College Boarding House. She is mentioned in her mother’s will (1895), along with her brother Charles, as having brought her to poverty.[ [census returns 1881, 1891; marriage index; clergy lists; Nethercot, First Five Lives of Annie Besant; Theosophical Yearbook 1933; Obituary in The Theosophist, 1903; info from Professor Joy Dixon]

He married (1873) Ann Catherine Johns. He was curate in charge of Wormleighton 1880-1 and vicar of Fotheringay 1881-1890, but had no cure by the 1891 volume of Crockfords, and was perhaps living apart from his wife. He disappears from the Clergy List c. 1900, reappears 1907, but is more continuous in Crockfords; he lived at 90 Canonbury Avenue until about 1933. [Crockfords, Clergy List, census returns 1871, 81, 91]

For a description of how her substantial contribution to the Cornwall section Victoria History of the Counties of England remained unpublished owing to the dilatoriness of another contributor, see John Beckett, [[otherbook:1116]\'Canon Thomas Taylor of St. Just and the Victoria County History in Cornwall, 1899-1938\'] Journal of the Royal Institution of Cornwall (2011) 31-44, 38-9. The Mr Moore mentioned in the 1840s is assumed to be Stephen Roger Moore, who married (Otterbourne 1823) FMY\'s first cousin Mary Kingsman (b.c. 1785). They evidently lived in or near Otterbourne.

The Mr and Mrs Moore mentioned in these early letters are perhaps the same as Mrs More who gave warm shawls to Otterbourne schoolchildren in December 1844;  Mrs Moore sent a parcel 24 Sept 1846 including Mr Kingsman\'s chain. All these references have therefore been rather boldly associated with Mary Kingsman, a niece of FMY\'s mother Mary (Kingsman) Bargus, daughter of her brother William George Kingsman (b.1755). The younger Mary Kingsman married (Otterbourne 1823) Stephen Roger Moore. In 1848 she proved the will of her uncle John Kingsman (1764-1848) who left legacies to her, FMY, JBY, CMY and the Rev. Thomas Westcombe. She can probably be identified with the Maria Kingsman mentioned in the CMY\'s autobiographical chapters (Coleridge, Life, 7), the orphan niece who was a member of the Bargus household during FMY\'s childhood. Details of the descendants of CMY\'s great-grandfather the Rev. Thomas Kingsman (1717-1779), Vicar of Botley, are at http://freepages.genealogy.rootsweb.ancestry.com/~kingsman/kingsman/england/indiI13063.html

The author of the ‘Garland for the Year’, who preserved the letters which shed such a useful light on the early history of MP, signed her contributions E. P. R. or Elizabeth P. Roberts. She may perhaps be identified with Elizabeth Piddocke Roberts (b. Kingswinford, Staffs. 1821) who published a book of verse in 1845. That person was the daughter of John Piddocke Roberts (b.1794/5) and his wife Susannah Maria Morris (b. 1789/90), who had been married at Kingswinford in 1819; he is described in the 1841 census of Armitage, Staffs. as a land agent, and in the 1851 Isle of Man census as a landed proprietor. By 1861 Elizabeth and her widowed mother were staying in West Bromwich, and she is described as a governess. Since the \'Garland\' author\'s father evidently died in 1859 it is likely they are one and the same. According to the IGI records she was one of at least ten children, of whom several died young. Survivors included Rebecca Surgy Roberts (b. 1831) who acted as a companion to a cousin in the Isle of Wight (1851, 1861 census), Phoebe Cordelia Roberts (1828-after 1881) and Martha Sarah Roberts (1835-1909) who married (1852) Thomas Oxenbould, a banker’s clerk. Roberts’s ‘Garland for the Year’ may possibly be the ‘semi botanical papers’ of which CMY wrote ‘I used to repent - of admitting them’. [1841 census, Armitage with Handsacre, Staffs.; parents Isle of Man 1851 census; 1861 census with cousin Lydia Morris, chemist, at West Bromwich; Oxenboulds, 1871, 1891 census, Handsworth; BMD indexes; IGI]

He married (1846 ) Isabella Margaret Saunders, [Parish, List of Carthusians R. L Arrowsmith, Charterhouse Register (1769-1872) 1974]
She was the mother of Olive Montagu Walford.
She was the daughter of Mrs Lucy Bethia Walford. [1881 census]

His contributions are all about the mission work of St. Luke’s, Burdett Road, Stepney; The Times (20 November 1915) records the dedication on 24 November of a chapel 'which has been added to St. Luke's Church, Burdett-road, Stepney as a memorial to the late Rev. Dr. William Wallace, who was vicar there for 44 years.’

description: principal of St. John’s Hall, Highbury
biography: He was author of The Names on the Gates of Pearl. He married (22 July 1865) Anna Maria Stubbs. He was tutor and then (1884) principal of St. John's Hall, Highbury, theological college.  His mother was the niece of Mary Martha Sherwood [ODNB]

He retired in 1851 as Lt-Col 3rd Bombay Light Cavalry. He married, first, Mary Emma Coulthard and, secondly (1853), Caroline Jeannette [or Janetta] Bignell, who married subsequently the Rev. James Beck. He was the son of W. Walter, and descended from John Walter the founder of The Times. His daughter Frances Walter married JBY; his daughter Gertrude lived with CMY from the 1870s; CMY also often mentions his daughters Mary (Walter) Woolcombe and Louisa (Walter) Halliday.  [BL OIOC MSS and East India Register Jan 1863; marriage index]

description: housemate of CMY, sister-in-law of JBY
biography: Daughter of Edward Walter and Mary Emma Coulthard. Her sister Frances married (1858) CMY\'s only brother Julian Bargus Yonge. She moved into Elderfield with CMY in about 1872.  Her illness began 8 years before 1871. [Bombay Baptisms N/3/24/118; \'she would have been 48 on the 24th\'] CMY described her movingly in ‘Our Tender Ones’ Mothers in Council 9 (January 1899) 20-27, 26: ‘Let me draw the picture of a real invalid not long passed away. She was a bright active girl of fourteen when rheumatic fever set in, followed by arthritis. Gradually, during nearly twenty years, every power was taken from her; first one knee was affected, then the other, then she could no longer sit at the piano, she moved on crutches, and drove in a donkey chaise; but in time, always after severe illness and pain, these pleasures failed her, she could only be carried from one room to another or to church on a couch. She lost her voice, and next the use of her right arm, and for several years was entirely confined to bed.’

description: half-brother of Gertrude Walter and of Frances (Walter) Yonge
biography: He appears in Alumni Oxoniensis as born 1855/6 which is consistent with the 1891 census, when he was with the Becks in Bildeston, described as MA Pembroke College Oxford and unmarried, although he could be the Herbert Simcoe Walter married in 1888 in Chelsea. [His death was reported in Trewman’s Exeter Flying Post 10 March 1897]

description: half-brother of Gertrude Walter and of Frances (Walter) Yonge
biography: He was gazetted to the 83rd Foot Regiment in 1875. He married Mabel Blanche Waller in July 1884. His death from an accident was reported in the Ipswich Journal 14 May 1885. He left a baby son, Edward Walter.

description: wife of the Rev. William Warburton.  Daughter of the 2nd Lord Ribblesdale
biography: she married (1853) the Rev. William Parsons Warburton.

He was educated at Balliol College, Oxford, and was a Fellow of All Souls 1849-53. He served as HM Inspector of Schools 1851-81, and of training schools 1881-5. He was an honorary Canon of Winchester 1878-81, and was made a Canon in 1885. He had three daughters Mary A. (b.1859/60), Katharine (b. 1861/2), and Charlotte (b. 1864/5) [Rugby School Register, Alumni Oxonienses]

description: member of the Gosling Society, novelist as ‘Mrs Humphry Ward
biography: Daughter of Thomas Arnold (1823-1900) school inspector and teacher, she was the granddaughter of Dr. Arnold of Rugby; she married (1872) Thomas Humphry Ward.  She became a Gosling as ‘Windermere’ in 1869;  she was evidently a friend of Theodora Clarke.

description: Vicar of Brixham and subsequently of Yealmpton
biography: He was ordained priest in 1888, and served from 1889 as Vicar of Brixham, Devon, until 1897 when he succeeded the Rev. George Woodhouse as Vicar of Yealmpton.  He married (1890) Edith Emma Morris.

His business was in High Street, Winchester (where it continues today, 2009, as a stationer). He was the recipient of payments from 1854, 1855,1856, 1857; he may have been the printer of The Little Duke. [1851, 61 census, register of deaths]

description: author of fiction and non-fiction as ‘S.W.’
biography: In the 1851 census she was living with her elder sister Selina Warren (b. 1812/3) at Hazlewood Farm, Hennock, near Bovey Tracey, Devon; she was staying with nephew William Henderson, woollen manufacturer, at 3 South Bailey Durham at the time of the 1861 census;  in the 1871 census she was again at Hazlewood, Hennock, with her eldest sister Charlotte Warren (b.1787/8).  It seems possible that in the 1860s she worked for the Rev. John Hawksley in Clifton as a governess.  She was author of fiction and non-fiction (tracts?) from 1860, under the initials S.W., for the SPCK.

The Miss Warren and Gundred referred to by CMY in 1900 were possibly Louisa Warren and her sister Gundred (b. Shropshire 1822/3) who appear in the 1891 census living at Market Drayton, but not in any earlier one, though a Georgiana Gundred Warren (birth registered Market Drayton 1839) appears with oddly varying dates of birth in the census returns. 

Unusual as Gundred is as a name, it was that of the wife (d.1085), of William de Warenne (d.1088), and therefore seems to have been chosen by people named Warren unexpectedly often.

description: Rector of Kentchurch, Herefordshire, contributor to MP (1870-82), local historian

biography: A pupil at St. Edward’s School, Oxford, in the 1881 census.

description: daughter of Catharine Elgie's first marriage

biography: In the 1881 census she is an authoress living with a widowed mother, teacher sister and bank clerk brother in Paddington;  in 1888 she is at at 10 Randolph Road Maida Vale.
Mentioned  (16 Jan 1854).

description: contributor to MP (1895), published as ‘the author of “Tip-Cat”’

biography: She may be the Miss White, later Mrs Gustard, dead by 1861, listed as a contributor to the Hursley Magazine in 1848. The latter was perhaps Margaretta Sarah White, daughter of the Rev. John White (1761/2-1841), Vicar of Exminster, who married (Mangalore 4 December 1850) Captain H. F. Gustard, 6th Regiment of Native Infantry (Morning Chronicle, 22 January 1851; Alumni Oxonienses). Or she may have been a member of the White family who occupied Ampfield House until at least the 1881 census, whose head in 1881 was another, different Rev. John White (b.Ampfield 1817). [Moor, Erminois, on Ampfield House]

description: widow of Thomas Fielder, railway porter
biography: She married (1850) Thomas Fielder (1812/3-1851). She is described by CMY as widowed and  dying of decline (15 March 1852), living at Bishopstoke.  She was the sister of Susan Whorley. They appear to have been daughters of Thomas Whorley (b. 1764/5), agricultural labourer, of Otterbourne. [1841, 51 censuses; marriage and death registers]

description: husband of Judith Whorley, railway porter

biography: They appear to have been daughters of James Whorley (b. 1764/5), agricultural labourer, of Otterbourne and his wife Jane (b.1778).  [1841, 51 censuses]
There were several families of Whorley or Worley living around Otterbourne in the 1841 census.
He was Rector of Compton from 1871; he was the third son of James Wickham, of Wonston, Hants.. [PO Hants 1875]

description: wife of the Rev. Charles Wickham, Rector of Compton
biography: This seems likely to be the ‘Mrs Wickham of Compton’ to whom CMY refers. [1891 census]

description: son of the Rev. Robert Wickham
biography: [Alumni Oxonienses]

description: wife of the Rev. Robert Wickham
biography: She lived with her brother, the Rev. Thomas Vowler Short, at Kingsworthy, Hants, from 1829-1834 when he was rector. She was born in Teignmouth, and her father the Rev William Short (d. 1829) was Archdeacon of Cornwall. [Short in ODNB]
He was master of Twyford School 1860-2, headmaster 1862-87 [Alumni Oxonienses]

description: daughter of the Rev. Robert Wickham
biography: mentioned (28 Oct 1844)

description: daughter of the Rev. Robert Wickham
biography: [1851 census]

He was subsequently Vicar of Gresford, Denbigh, 1847. He was third son of William Wickham of Winchester [Alumni Oxonienses] He is found in the 1851 census at Gresford with his wife Jane Susannah, 52; daughters Elizabeth Ann, 18; and Laura Maria, 6; in the 1871 census with wife Jane Susannah, 72 b. Teignmouth, daughter Laura Maria, 26, and brother in law Thomas Vowler Short (1790-1872) late Bp of St Asaph, 80.
Brother-in-law of the Rev. Robert Wickham, he lived at Kingsworthy with his sister 1829-34 when he was Rector there.

description: son of Rev. Robert Wickham, Vicar of Rossett, Shropshire
biography: [Alumni Oxonienses]

description: wife of the Rev. Alfred Wigan
biography: She married (1855) the Rev. Alfred Wigan (b.1818), Rector of Luddesdown;  they had six daughters and employed a governess during the 1881 census.

Youngest son of William Wilberforce (1759-1833), he married Mary Sargent (1811-1878), whose sisters had married Manning and his brother Samuel Wilberforce. He was Vicar of Deal and then East Farleigh before he followed his wife into the Roman Catholic church on 15 September 1850.

He married, first, Agnes Wrangham (d. 1834) and, secondly (1837), Jane Legard (d.1853); he was  appointed Archdeacon of the East Riding in 1841;  and received into the Roman Catholic church 31 October 1853.
He married (1828) Emily Sargent (1807-1841);  he served as Bishop of Oxford from December 1845 and, Bishop of Winchester from 1869 to his death [ODNB]

She was the fifth of seven daughters (there were also four sons); she was living in Chester with her mother and sisters in the 1861 and with her sisters in the 1881 census; a friend of Mrs Moberly; she contributed to CMY’s Musings over the Christian Year. Her brother Richard Wilbraham was governor of the Royal Victoria Hospital, Netley. [LG 1906 Wilbraham of Delamere]

description: Governor of the Royal Hospital, Netley
biography: He married (1846) Eliza Frances Egerton and had one daughter, Katherine (Wilbraham) Baker-Wilbraham. He was confirmed as an adult after instruction by Keble, and may have inspired the episode in The Young Stepmother. His papers are in Cheshire Record Office.

Margaret Wilcox was the daughter of William Wilcox (1813-1872), Collector of Customs, and his wife Mary Anne Marwood (1813-1870), half-sister of the Rev. Charles Dodgson (1800-1868), father of Lewis Carroll.

They lived at Whitburn, Northumberland, near CMY\'s friends the Harrisons.  There were 14 children, of which she was the third.
Perhaps William Edward Wilcox (1835-1876), brother of Margaret Wilcox and cousin and friend of Lewis Carroll.

description: novelist, contributor to MP (1866-83), member of the Gosling Society
biography: Daughter of Major-General Edmund Neal Wilford (1800-1881), RA, Governor of the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, until his retirement, she was a Gosling as ‘Turkscap’ from June 1865; her address then was c/o Mrs Chrystall\'s,. St. Cross, Winchester. In the 1851 census, she was 15 and was staying at Bromley Kent, in the company of Maria Cristall, whom CMY describes as her aunt.  In 1881 she and her elder sister Emma, 48, were living with their father in St. Leonards; in 1891 she and Emma were staying in Bournemouth.  Her Royal Literary Fund file indicates that she had suffered from mental illness intermittently since 1883 and was in a private asylum in 1889 when CMY wrote a letter to them on her behalf.  (Her application was refused on the grounds ‘authorship insufficient’, which seems rather harsh since she had published sixteen books since 1858.)  CMY assured Bullock (16 March 1895) that she was well and at home with her sister.  She was probably the Florence Wilford who died at Keynsham, Glos. in 1897. [IGI; RLF application 2311, born at Woolwich]
He served in the Royal Artillery and was Governor of the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich; he died at his residence at St. Leonard's on Sea, . [The Times, 19 Dec 1881 9f; ]
[ODNB]

description: 'a young lady whom I know very well'
Rector of Campton, uncle of Ann Carter Smith
biography: He was educated at Clare College, Cambridge, succeeded his father as Rector of Campton 1839-64 and founded the Bedford Library; uncle of Ann Carter Smith. [Alumni Cantabrigienses]

description: Rector of Sutton Coldfield, uncle of Ann Carter Smith
biography: Educated at Westminster and Trinity College, Cambridge, priest 1829, Headmaster of Westminster School 1828-1846, Rector of Sutton Coldfield 1844-50, Vicar of Pershore 1850-66, Hon. Canon of Worcester; he married (1833) Anne Gray, daughter of the Bishop of Bristol, uncle of Ann Carter Smith. [Alumni Cantabrigienses]

description: Rector of Datchworth, uncle of Ann Carter Smith
biography: He was educated at Westminster and Clare College, Cambridge, 2nd Wrangler, Fellow of Clare 1827-50, barrister 1830-39, ordained 1841; he married  (1850) Jane Ferguson; he was Rector of Datchworth 1849-74. [Alumni Cantabrigienses]

description: Vicar of Portsea, third son of the Rev. Robert Wilson, Vicar of Rownhams
biography: A scholar of Keble College, Oxford. [Alumni Oxonienses ; obituary The Times, 18 October 1909]

description: son of the Rev. Robert Francis Wilson
biography: graduated Oxford, barrister, married Annie C. G. ---  (b.1851/2); collected stamps as a little boy.  [Vital Records, 1861, 1871, 1881 census].

description: second son of the Rev. Robert Francis Wilson
biography: He married (1882) Helen Margaret Heath. [The Times 21 September 1882]

description: wife of the Rev. Robert Francis Wilson
biography: She married (6 May 1847) the Rev. Robert Francis Wilson, Vicar of Rownhams (d. 1888).  The Court and Lady’s Magazine (April 1847) 57 has ‘Trench, Maria, d. of the rev. Frederick S. Trench and lady Helen Trench, of Kilmorony, to the rev. Francis Wilson, son of Thomas Wilson esq. formerly M. P. for the city of London; at the parish church of Athy, by the rev. John Keble, vicar of Hursley Hants, May 6 [1847]’ She was 1st cousin of T.R.F. Cooke Trench and, through her mother, of Sir William Heathcote\'s children by his first marriage. Frances Dorothy (Grimston) Moor was her first cousin, daughter of her aunt Jane Trench. [PB 1914 Ashtown; Erminois]
She was on the circulation list for The Trial.

He married (6 May 1847) Maria Trench (1820/1-7 Dec 1908). He was educated at Oriel College, Oxford, and served as curate of Hursley, then curate of Ampfield from April 1841; he resigned Ampfield in October 1853; he was perpetual curate of Baldersby Yorks 1858-63, and vicar of Rownhams 1863; he left issue [PB 1914 Ashtown; Clergy List]

description: Rector of the English College in Rome
biography: He was president of Oscott College, Cardinal Archbishop of Westminster 1850.

description: youngest brother of the Rev. William Bigg Wither
curate of Otterbourne to 1871 and subsequently Rector of Hardwick, Bucks.
biography: His father Harris Bigg Wither had proposed to Jane Austen. [R. F. Bigg-Wither, Materials for a History of the Wither Family Winchester, Warren 1907]

description: nephew of the Rev. William Bigg Wither
biography: He was fifth child of Mr Bigg Wither's eldest brother; (22 July 1845) 'a very nice little boy of nine years old' ;  lost at sea. [LG 1871]

description: sister of the Rev. William Bigg Wither
biography: She shared a birthday with CMY.  She lived with her sister Margaret in Southgate St., Winchester.

description: wife of the Rev. Algernon Wodehouse
biography: She married (1844) the Rev. Algernon Wodehouse, Rector of Easton, near Winchester;  she was aunt of the poet Swinburne and of Mrs Disney Leith.
He married (1844) Lady Eleanor Ashburnham (d.1895).
A Gosling as Thistle in 1867, her address 50 Westbourne Park, London.
The Literary Year Book (1901), 239, lists \'WOOD, MISS FRANCES HARIOTT, Elmwood, 116 Bromley Road, Beckenham, Kent.\' She published both fiction and plays between the 1870s and 1920s.

Eldest of the ten children of the Rev, Henry Arthur Woodgate, Rector of Bellbroughton, Worcs., she was living in Crowthorne with three unmarried younger sisters at the time of the 1891 census.  She was a friend and correspondent of  [[person:1084]John Henry Newman] (was she perhaps his goddaughter?).
[tablet in All Saints, Sparkwell]
Daughter of WCY’s sister Anne (Yonge) Pode, she married (30 July 1861) William John Woollcombe (1832-1913).

description: brother of Robert and  William Woollcombe
sister of Gertrude Walter and of Frances (Walter) Yonge
biography: She \'turned 25 in 1870\', and married (1871) Major Robert Woollcombe (1835-1920).

He married (1871) Mary Walter, whose sister Frances was married to CMY\'s brother JBY, and whose sister Gertrude Walter lived with CMY.  He came from a gentry family settled near Puslinch and his brother was married to Anne Catharina Pode, who was a cousin, niece of WCY.

description: brother of Robert and Richard Woollcombe
biography: He married (1861) Anne Catharina Pode (d. 1913), cousin of CMY and sister of Charlotte Cordelia (Pode) Yonge.

description: brother of William, Richard and Robert Woollcombe
brother of William, Richard and Robert Woollcombe
Bishop of St Andrews, Dunkeld and Dunblane
biography: He became bishop in 1852. Before that he had travelled in France with Roundell Palmer in 1834, and married (1835) Charlotte Day, who died giving birth to a daughter Charlotte Emmeline (b. 1839). He was second master of Winchester College 1835-1846, and author of Christian Boyhood at a Public School (1846). He was first headmaster of Trinity College Glenalmond, 1847. He married, secondly (28 October 1846), Katharine Mary Barter (d. 23 Apr 1897), eldest daughter of the Rev. William Barter, Rector of Burghclere, and niece of Warden Barter; he had 12 children by his second marriage. Like the Rt. Rev. Christopher Wordsworth, Bishop of Lincoln, he was a son of the poet’s brother Christopher, master of Trinity College, Cambridge. [ODNB]
He married (6 December 1838) Susanna Hatley Frere (1811-1884);  he was father of Elizabeth Wordsworth, brother of the Rt. Rev. Charles Wordsworth, and nephew of the poet. [LG 1952, LG 1871]

description: contributor to MP (1871-1893), principal of Lady Margaret Hall
biography: Daughter of the Rt. Rev. Christopher Wordsworth, she was appointed Lady Principal of Lady Margaret Hall in 1878. She contributed a poem to MP in 1871 under the name \'VERITAS\' and probably was the author of another 16 poems which appeared under that pseudonym to February 1883. [Battiscombe, Reluctant Pioneer]

Brother of Elizabeth Wordsworth, he married first (1870), Susan Esther Coxe (daughter of the Rev. Henry Coxe), with whom he had two children, and, secondly (1896), Mary Anne Frances William, and had four sons and two daughters.

description: daughter of the Rev. William Barter
biography: She was the eldest daughter of the Rev. William Barter, Rector of Burghclere, and niece of the Rev. Robert Speckott Barter (1790-1861), Warden of Winchester College.  She married (28 October 1846), as his second wife, the Rev. Charles Wordsworth. She is not to be confused with her cousin Kate Barter, or the latter’s sister-in-law, Kitty (Moberly) Barter.

description: first wife of the Rt. Rev. [[person:1567]John Wordsworth]
biography: She was the daughter of the Rev. [[person:377]Henry Octavius Coxe].
Head of the College of Greyladies which did social work in Southwark. [Wordsworth, Glimpses of the Past]
He was a JP, and retired from the Bengal Civil Service; he was dead by 1914. [his son in PB 1914; census 1891]
[death index; 1891 census]

The Miss Yards were residents of Otterbourne 1848, 1859, 1861, living in Winchester Kingsgate St 1864 and 1871, and in 1881 with brother Frederick Yard 58, major in army;  they were friends of Elizabeth Sewell.

description: aunt of CMY, half-sister of FMY
biography: Known as ‘Aunt Yonge’, she married (25 March 1813) the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch.

description: fourth daughter of Rev. Duke Yonge of Puslinch

biography: Closest friend of CMY, she shared her birthday with her sister Alethea [Coleridge, Life, 66]

Son of the Rev. Duke Yonge, Vicar of Antony, he married (1870) Lucy Williams (d.1879). He was educated at Exeter College, Oxford, became a landscape artist, had one daughter Alethea Yonge (b. Italy 1870/1). He may have become a Roman Catholic like his brother John. [Alumni Oxonienses, Coleridge, Life 69]

description: uncle of CMY, master at Eton
biography: He married (4 Dec 1810) Elizabeth Lord (d. 11 Jan 1868).  He was father of Charles Duke Yonge, the writer (whom CMY never mentions, why?) and of the Rev. John Eyre Yonge.
First cousin of CMY, she was daughter of WCY’s sister Anne (Yonge) Pode.  She married (26 Aug 1862) Rev. Duke Yonge (1823-1881), of Puslinch. [census, LG]
Daughter of the Rev. John Eyre Yonge, her address at death was Cotswold, Station Road, Brading Isle of Wight; probate was granted to Catherine Mildred Leser wife of Karl Frederick Leser [will]

The daughter of William Hay of Duns Castle and Mary Garstin, she was connected to the Puslinch Yonges, her mother being a first cousin of Lord Seaton, Cordelia (Colborne) Yonge and Alethea Henrietta (Bargus) Yonge.  She married (28 June 1848) John Bargus Yonge of Puslinch (1821-1863). [LGI 1914 Garstin of Braganstown]

description: CMY’s ‘Aunt Duke’, wife of the Rev. Duke Yonge
biography: Sister of Lord Seaton, half-sister of Alethea Henrietta (Bargus) Yonge and stepsister of FMY, she married (14 May 1806) the Rev. Duke Yonge (1779-1836), Vicar of Antony.
She died of whooping cough aged 16 months. [Pall Mall Gazette 16 December 1865]

description: third daughter of the Rev. Duke Yonge of Puslinch
biography: She married (1903) the Ven. Cyril Price (1866-1943).

He was Vicar of Broxted, Essex 1869-85, and Vicar of Boreham, Essex 1885-.  Not himself related to CMY, he married Mary Isabel Yonge, daughter of her cousin the Rev. John Eyre Yonge, and they had Frederick, b. 1874/5, Philip Caynton, b. 1877/8, Denys Nelson b. 1880, Isabel, b. 1882/3 and Horace b. 1883/4.
He was the third son of the Rev. Duke Yonge of Puslinch and Charlotte Pode.  He married (1894) Isabella Sydney Bowen.  His elder brother Charles married her sister Catherine Ada Helena Bowen in 1899.

He was grandson of the Rev. Duke Yonge (1809-1846), Vicar of Antony, and son of the Rev. Duke John Yonge.  He (and ?three brothers) were living with their grandmother Cordelia (Colborne) Yonge at the time of the 1851 census.

The son of Rev. Duke Yonge, Vicar of Antony, he married (1840) Elizabeth Roberts, who married, secondly, Captain Scott;  his three sons were Duke Dowton Yonge, R.N., Kenneth Duke Yonge and Walter Duke Yonge. [The 1851 census suggests there was another, James]

description: Vicar of Antony, paternal uncle of CMY
biography: Eldest brother of WCY, he married (14 May 1806) Cordelia Anne Colborne, who was FMY’s stepsister.

The fourth and only surviving of the five sons of the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch, and Alethea Henrietta (Bargus) Yonge, he inherited Puslinch in 1877 (John, James, John Bargus and Edmund Charles having predeceased him).  He was curate of Newton Ferrars in 1849, and subsequently Rector of Newton Ferrars like his father.  He married (26 Aug 1862) Charlotte Cordelia Pode (1839/40-7 Sept 1929), who was his second cousin (she was CMY's first cousin).  He shared two of her eight great-grandparents, whereas he shared four of CMY's eight great-grandparents.  According to a letter of his youngest daughter Alethea’s, he had wished to marry CMY.

description: Vicar of Cornwood, paternal grandfather of CMY.
biography: He served as Vicar of Cornwood 1793-1811.  He married (12 Mar 1777) Catherine, sister of Sir Thomas Crawley-Boevey.

Known as Charles Yonge, he was the fifth son of Rev John Yonge of Puslinch and Alethea Bargus, CMY describes him as  \'born on my birthday in 1827\' [a tablet in Newton Ferrars church says \'d. Jan 15 1847 aged 19 years\']

description: younger brother of the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch
biography: He married (1835) Jane Ley Bennett, and had one son, James Edmund (b.1843).

description: member of the Gosling Society, cousin of CMY
biography: A Gosling as ‘Cricket’  1865-after 1869, she was daughter of the Rev. John Eyre Yonge, master at Eton, who was CMY’s first cousin.  Charlotte Fortescue Yonge was her sister.
Known as Frances, she married (9 Sept 1858) Julian Bargus Yonge (1830-1891). [India Office, Bombay Baptisms]
Youngest daughter of the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch, she seems to have been retarded following childhood measles [tomb Newton Ferrars church]

FMY married (25 Oct 1822) William Crawley Yonge.  [Hampshire: - Marriage License allegations, Bishop of Winchester, 1689-1837 has: Yonge, William-Crawley, of Cornwood, co. Devon, gent., b., s. of Duke & Catherine Yonge, bap. 26 Jun 1795 , at C., by affidavit of John Yonge, of Puslink, co. Devon, clerk, & Frances-Mary Bargus, of Otterbourne, dau. of Thomas and Mary Bargus, b. 13 Jan , bap. 14 Jan 1793 , at St. Michael's, Winchester, at O., 23 Oct 1822.]
He emigrated to the U.S.A. and married (1892) Edith Louise Isabel Shortride; they adopted a daughter Gwendolene Violet Yonge, who married – Jones. (two says Ian Yonge)
Son of the Rev. Duke Yonge, Vicar of Antony, he was dismissed in disgrace for going AWOL 1855, emigrated to New Zealand, married (1859)  Charlotte Andrews (d. 1922), and has living descendants.
Son of the Rev. Duke Yonge of Puslinch and Charlotte Pode, when he died he was in deacon’s orders only, [Win Coll Reg, LG 1952]

Son  of JBY.  He was killed at Rhodes Drift, Crocodile River, in what is now Zimbabwe, during the Boer War.  Recorded as a medical student aged 19 in 1881 census, probably in mistake for his brother Arthur, he emigrated to Rhodesia and also served in the Matabele War of 1896. [wills index, left £4881)

He was treasurer of the county of Southampton, and son of CMY's Eton uncle.  He married (6 Oct 1859) Lucy Acland (Camberwell 1819-1902) daughter of Gideon Acland, lived at Stoke Lodge, Bishopstoke, formerly home of his elder brother James Arthur Yonge and Hannah (Rogers) Yonge, later Carey.

description: adopted daughter of Francis Arthur Yonge
biography: She proved his will; she was married to a man named Jones.
[Birth register; Morning Post 30 October 1860; Times 19 June 1941].

He married, first (12 Jan 1820), his cousin Margaret Crawley (d. 22 Apr 1867), daughter of Sir Thomas Crawley-Boevey, 3rd Bt. He married secondly (25 Aug 1868), Anna Susanna Couch (1801-1894).  The children of his first marriage, James \'a few months older than myself, Eleonora, and Edward, the last born in 1827\' all died in 1830. [DNB, LG, Coleridge, Life 67, Death index, census returns]

description: cousin of CMY, second and eldest surviving son of the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch
biography: Known as 'Jemmy Jummy' CMY wrote that he was 'a kind of special patron of mine';  he died at Otterbourne aged 18 [Coleridge, Life 65; tablet in Newton Ferrars church]
Third dau of Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch and Alethea Henrietta Bargus. [tomb Newton Ferrars Church]

description: cousin of CMY, eldest son of Rev. Duke Yonge of Puslinch
biography: He inherited Puslinch in 1881 and married (1899) Vera Vaughan Holberton.

description: eldest son of the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch
third son of the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch
biography: He married (28 June 1848), his second cousin Cordelia Hay, daughter of William Hay of Dunse Castle.  He died at Biarritz. CMY wrote of his  'sullen, rather whiny temper'. [Coleridge, Life 65, LG]

Son of the Rev. Charles Yonge, he was a master at Eton,  locum tenens in Otterbourne in 1872.  He married (19 Dec 1844) the Hon. Catherine Charlotte Lysaght (1822-1905).  He was father of Elizabeth Catherine and of Charlotte Fortescue Yonge.

description: wife of the Rev. John Eyre Yonge
biography: Sometimes her letters are confused with CMY’s in libraries.

The son of the Rev. Duke Yonge, Vicar of Antony, he married first (Brussels 12 August 1839) a widow with two children, Elizabeth Alice (Holmes) Reed (1799/1800-1863) and, secondly (1864) Mary Jones.  He seems to have converted to Roman Catholicism.  For that reason he was not welcome at WCY’s funeral. By his first marriage he had three sons, Francis Arthur Holmes Yonge, James Frederick Moore Yonge (b. Coblentz 1841/2?) and Stephen Duke Yonge (Coblentz 1844/5-1914). In the 1871 census he and his second wife are living in Cornwall with three small grandsons, born in Mauritius, and probably the children of Francis, who had gone to live there. The two younger sons had moved to Melbourne, Australia, by 1864. One of the \'grandsons\', Eugene Yonge (b. Mauritius 1867/8) appears in the 1881 census in Plymstock with his uncle the Rev. Theophilus Jones (1822/3-1886), Vicar of Bradstone, and as a medical student in the 1891 census. [census; Alumni Oxonienses An obituary of \'Eugene Stephen Yonge, M.D.Edin., Physician, Manchester Hospital For Consumption\' appeared in the The British Medical Journal 1 (Feb. 3, 1912), p. 280; advertisement Morning Post 16 April 1864, 1]

Rector of Newton Ferrars and squire of Puslinch, he was first cousin once removed and uncle by marriage of CMY.  His father was uncle to WCY, and he married (25 March 1813) Alethea Henrietta Bargus, half-sister of FMY.

He was educated at Eton and Balliol College Oxford (BA 1853). He joined the Rifle Brigade 1851, entered the Middle Temple 1855. He married (9 Sept 1858) Emma Frances Walter (1839-1913). He was a J.P. for Hampshire; sold Otterbourne House to Major Robert Scarlett in 1891 and died ‘a few days later’ (John Keble’s Parishes, 149), at 70 Kensington Gardens Square in the presence of his son Maurice [death certificate] but according to the probate of his will at 2 Radnor Place Hyde Park.

description: cousin and aunt by marriage of CMY
biography: She married (1820) her cousin Dr. James Yonge.  She was the daughter of Sir Thomas Crawley-Boevey, 2nd Bt..  Her three children all died in 1830, after which she never left the house except for church. [In the census returns she is 45 in 1841 and 62 in 1851??]
Second daughter of the Rev. John Yonge and Alethea Henrietta Bargus, she was the last surviving of their ten children.
Known as 'Aunt Marianne', she was the sister of the Rev. John Yonge of Puslinch.
The second daughter of the Rev. John Eyre Yonge, she married (1872), the Rev. Denys Nelson Yonge, Vicar of Boreham, Chelmsford (no relation). [LG 1952]

Daughter of Lt-Col Woods of Llandaff, Glamorgan, she married (1899) Maurice Edward Yonge.  Her address was Lincolns, Boyatt Lane, Eastleigh, her estate was £157  and probate was granted to Maurice Yonge [will]

He seems to have trained as an engineer.  He married (19 Apr 1899) Maude Woods (d.1938).  He died at St Faiths, Merdon Avenue, Chandlers Ford, Eastleigh, Probate was granted at Bristol 5 June 1940 to George Hubert Woods and Henry Jex Woods  for £221 4s. He went to Stubbington House school, near Fareham, a naval preparatory school. [1881 census; will]

He married (25 Oct 1822) Frances Mary Bargus.
His funeral was held on Saturday 4 March 1854.

He died as a baby. Coleridge gives his names as William Keble Yonge (Keble was his godfather) but his birth and death were evidently registered as William Coulthard Yonge.  His maternal grandmother was born Mary Emma Coulthard.

description: first cousin and ward of Charlotte Keble
biography: She married (20 Oct 1839) Rev. Peter Young. They had children James 7, John 5, William 4, Mary 2 and Elizabeth 1 in 1851 census; in 1871 George Edward 19 Frederick Coxwell 8, Mary Jane 22, Elizabeth Ann 21, Charlotte Lucy 17; in 1881 Mary Jane 32 and Charlotte L 27; the last two still living with their father in Lincoln in 1901. [Recollections of the Rev. Peter Young, M.A., late Rector of North Witham, Lincolnshire and Canon of Lincoln, edited by his daughter (Grimsby: Albert Gait 1903), a pamphlet in London Library]

CMY calls him Jimmy Young. Brother of the Rev. Peter Young, he succeeded Keble as Vicar of Hursley, 1866; he had a wife Anna (b. Ilfracombe 1824/5), and children Frances (b. Brigstock Northants 1850/1), Elspeth Jane (b. 1853/4), Harry Gavin (b. Scotland 1854/5), Anna Edith (b. 1856/7), Louisa Caroline (b. 1858/9) and Marion Jemima (b. 1859/60). [1861, 81 census, Recollections of the Rev. Peter Young]
He was the son of the Rev. Peter Young, Rector of North Witham. [Recollections of the Rev. Peter Young, 1851 census]

He served as curate of Hursley from 1841, but Bishop Sumner refused to ordain him, so he moved away in 1861 to become Rector of North Witham, Lincolnshire.  He married (20 Oct 1839) Mrs Keble’s ward and cousin Caroline Coxwell.

She was a Gosling as Mignonette 1866/7-?9, her address 23 Maryon Road, Woolwich, and she was probably this person, who was daughter of Lt Gen. C. W. Younghusband (1821-1899), Superintendent of Royal Gun Factories, Woolwich.  If so, she married (1871) Lt.-Col. George O'Malley.  She was accused by C.R. Coleridge of carelessly mislaying the Barnacle [LG 1906 Younghusband, O'Malley].
Daughter of the 2nd Lord Heytesbury, she appears to have joined the Wantage Sisterhood.  She subscribed to The Net.

It is possible that CMY\'s Miss Cox is the same as the Agnes Cox who published Zenza and Ounah, the Indian sisters, and other poems (Windermere: Johnson 1887). Miss Cox evidently knew the author of [[otherbook:612]\'The Cardioscope\'], an early series in MP, and perhaps that was written by [[person:375]Harriet Lucy Cox], who is a probable early contributor. However, there is little substantial evidence here.
He was an old boy of Winchester College and published extensively on that subject, on bibliography and on local history.

The son of Sir Martin Crawley Boevey, 4th Bt., who was CMY\'s second cousin, he published a biography, The Perverse Widow, of Catharina (Riches) Boevey (1670-1726), to whose husband they were related. He was the brother of Sybella Crawley Boevey.
She was connected by marriage to the Crawley family, to which CMY\'s paternal grandmother belonged.

She had a younger sister named Edith Pond, who was housemaid to Maurice Yonge at the time of the 1901 census (just after CMY\'s death).  They were the daughters of Francis Pond, cabinet-maker, of Wantage.
He served as Bishop of Melanesia (1894-1911) in succession to the Rt. Rev. J. R. Selwyn, and then as Bishop of Bunbury, Australia, 1918-1937.

description: novelist and founder of the Society of Authors
biography: He was knighted in 1895.

He was loathed and mistrusted by CMY, no doubt because, being High Church and having begun as a Conservative, he should have known better than to associate with liberals and advocates of non-denominational education.

title: Ctss of Macclesfield
biography: She married (1842) the 6th Earl of Macclesfield (1811-1896) and had 15 children.  Her husband was succeeded by a grandson who did not marry till 1909, so she must be the person referred to.

description: Rector of Newton Ferrars, cousin of CMY
biography: He was the son of the Rev. Duke Yonge of Puslinch and of Charlotte Cordelia Pode, who were both first cousins of CMY, on her mother\'s and father\'s sides respectively, and were each other\'s second cousins.  Charles Yonge married (1899) Catherine Ada Helena Bowen.  He is remembered for the collection of rare crocuses he naturalized in the churchyard at Newton Ferrars.

description: probably a member of the Spider Society as \'Bath Brick\'
biography:
Daughter of Richard Woodward (d.1875), retired Bengal Civil Service, she lived in Bath in 1871 and 1881
and 1891 with her widowed mother at the Knoll, Clevedon.  She was a fellow
of the Royal Meterological Society, a member of the Ex Libris Society
(collecting bookplates), and a supporter of local history societies and
publications. She contributed a memoir of her uncle Vincent Stuckey Lean to
his book on proverbs (1902-4). She compiled the autograph album in which the
letters to Bath Brick were found;  since Bath Brick is known to have lived
near Clevedon they were probably the same person.

The European Magazine 14 (1788) 231 recorded the marriage of Samuel Leake, esq., of the Isle of Wight, to Sophia Bargus, youngest daughter of Richard Bargus esq. of Fareham. She appears to have been a half-sister of the Rev. Thomas Bargus. The Gentleman’s Magazine 182 (1847) 563 records her death at Cheltenham aged 85, spelling it Leeke, and stating that she was the mother of Captain Sir Henry Leeke, R.N. (1794-1870, ODNB,/i>). Lady Tucker, to whom CMY refers, would thus be her daughter and FMY’s first cousin.

The Gentleman’s Magazine (1806) 760 records the death of the widow of Dr. Bogue, of Fareham, eldest daughter of Richard Bargus of Fareham.  If she was the Mary Bargus christened at Fareham in 1746 she was the child of Richard Bargus’s first wife Frances Eyer, and thus probably a full sister of CMY\'s maternal grandfather the Rev. Thomas Bargus. She was probably married at Fareham in 1775, though the IGI transcribes her husband’s name as Bogrie. The Rev. John Richard Bogue, whom CMY describes as her cousin, was probably her grandson.
The daughter of Richard Bargus and Ann Lock, she was christened at Fareham in 1761, and may have died young.

CMY describes him as \'a naval officer, who after sailing round the world with Lord Anson, had settled at Fareham, in Hampshire\' (Coleridge, Life 4). He died in his 83rd year at Fareham (Gentleman’s Magazine, 1805, 389). He married, first (Rowner 1745), Frances Eyer and, secondly (Fareham 1759), Ann Lock. His second wife’s death is also recorded in the Gentleman’s Magazine (1814) 87. According to the Hampshire Allegations for marriage licences they were 36 and 25 at marriage. It appears from the IGI that the Rev. Thomas Bargus (christened Fareham 1753) and Mary (Bargus) Bogue were the children of his first marriage, Sophia (Bargus) Leeke, Charlotte Bargus and John Lock Bargus (b. 1762/3) of the second. There may have been other children.

Son of Richard Bargus and Ann Lock, and half-brother of CMY’s grandfather the Rev. Thomas Bargus. CMY in Coleridge, Life, 6 states that he died in the same epidemic as Lord Brooke (1772-1786), son of the 2nd Earl of Warwick and his first wife Georgiana Peachey (whose father Lord Selsey was Thomas Bargus’s patron). John Lock Bargus appears in Alumni Oxonienses and Register of Gray’s Inn.

title: Lady Leconfield
description: Daughter of the Lady Dalmeny whose picture CMY admired, she married (1867) the 1st Lord Leconfield and had nine children.
member of the Gosling Society as Bessie (or Befsie)
biography: This letter was found in the Guille autograph album, and was almost certainly addressed to one of the eight daughters of the Rev. George de Cartaret Guille, Rector of Torrington, and his wife Sophia Stevens, heiress of Cross, near Torrington.  The most likely candidate seems to be the third sister, Charlotte Esther Sophia Guille  Other possibilities among the sisters are the eldest, Louisa Margaret A. Guille (b. 1849) who m. (1877) the Rev. Frederick Colby and then (1905) William Secker; or the second, Marian Elizabeth Guille (1851-1931) who married (1881) William George Le Cocq, RN (1842/3-1913).  Their younger sister Rosa Caroline (b.1858) became (1878) the wife of the poet William Johnson Cory.

Grandfather of Christabel Rose Coleridge.  CMY was not related to him, but to his sister-in-law Frances Duke (Taylor) Coleridge (1760-1838), wife of his brother James (1759-1836).  Frances Duke Coleridge was first cousin of CMY\'s grandfather the Rev. Duke Yonge, their mothers being sisters called Duke.
Since CMY indicates she wrote from Ramsgate Vicarage, she was presumably the wife of the Rev. Canon Harry Bartram, Vicar of Ramsgate.

biography: No relation to CMY, this lady is all the same the key to the complex cousinhood which surrounded her.  She had two children, John and Cordelia Anne, by her first marriage to Samuel Colborne.  She then married the Rev. Thomas Bargus, and died giving birth to their daughter Alethea Henrietta Bargus.  He remarried, and had a daughter, CMY\'s mother Frances Mary Bargus.   Cordelia Colborne married the Rev. Duke Yonge.  Alethea married the latter\'s cousin the Rev John Yonge.  John Colborne married Elizabeth Yonge (sister of the Rev. John Yonge). Lastly, Frances married William Crawley Yonge (brother of the Rev. Duke Yonge).
Sister of the transported rioter Joseph Mason (1799-1863), she may be the \'poor Mason (Mrs Reeves)\' referred to in 1844, and possibly also the nurse who married a drum major mentioned in 1864.

Rector of Sarsden, father of Catherine Barter

biography: He was subsequently Vicar of Littlemore 1851-72. He was undoubtedly a relation (grandson?, great-nephew?) of the Rt. Rev. George Isaac Huntingford (1748-1832), Bishop of Hereford and Warden of Winchester College.

The references by Anne Yonge to Lady Georgiana Bulteel are mysterious, but may refer to Lady Elizabeth Bulteel, who married (1826) John Crocker Bulteel, a landowner near Puslinch.

Elizabeth Yonge, sister of CMY\'s grandfather the Rev. Duke Yonge, married a local landowner, Philip Morshead of Widey Court, Egg Buckland, Plymouth.  They had an only daughter Elizabeth Morshead, who married Colonel Anderson and had 11 children called Anderson Morshead.  Of these the heir, the Rev. John Philip Anderson Morshead married (1845)his second cousin Alethea Yonge of Puslinch, Pentire was the father of Mary Anderson Morshead.  Their sister Elizabeth Morshead, referred to by Anne Yonge, died in Devon in 1849. [Burke LG 1871; death register]

Elder sister of [[person:97]Anne Baker], she was the daughter of Major Thomas Richard Baker (1802-1884), J.P., 7th Fusiliers, Rtd. and Mary Frances Anderson Morshead (d. 1843), whose grandmother Elizabeth Yonge was a sister of CMY\'s grandfather. [LG 1906 Baker of Bayfordbury for parents]
Younger sister of CMY\'s grandmother, she married (1784) Nicholas Westcombe and had a son, the Rev. Thomas Westcombe.
Son of Sarah (Kingsman) Westcombe, his mother and FMY\'s were sisters.
He had several brothers of whom one was CMY\'s friend the Rev. William Parsons Warburton.
Marianne Small (b. 1839/40) and Elizabeth Small (b. 1837/8) were the daughters of John Small (b. 1797/8), of Allbrook, agricultural labourer.

Elizabeth (Holmes) Reed married, as her third husband, CMY\'s cousin Dr. John Francis Duke Yonge, son of the Rev. Duke Yonge of Antony, who was about 14 years her junior: they had three sons: Francis Arthur Holmes Yonge, James Frederick Moore Yonge, and Stephen Duke Yonge. He became a Roman Catholic in the late 1840s, to the consternation of his family, but according to CMY, she did not. [ Her marriage, under the name Elizabeth Bird Alice Reed, is recorded in Brussels, 1839 by the IGI; advertisement for administration of estate of J.V.C. Reed in the Morning Post 16 April 1864, 1] She was the daughter of Richard Holmes, of Westcott, St. Dominick, Cornwall, and Elizabeth Nash. She was first married (18 November 1815), aged not quite 16, in the church at Antony, Cornwall, to Cavalie Shorthouse Mercer (1789-1819), with whom she had two children, Theodosia Alice Sterling Mercer (1817-1832) and Henrietta Fyers (Mercer) Muller (1818-1839). He died in Bermuda, leaving her a widow of 19. She remarried (1822) Captain John Reed (d. 1835) with whom she had at least six children, including Eliza Holmes Reed, who married Thomas C. Watson, and John Vaughan Carden Reed (d. 1858) Lieutenant in the Royal Marine Light Infantry. She had perhaps known the much younger John Francis Duke Yonge since his childhood, since he had been brought up in Antony. Information from Mr Graeme Hicks.
Mentioned as a friend of the Anderson Morsheads, condoling with them on the birth of a fifth son.
He served as bishop from 1827 to his death and was unpopular and eccentric.

He was consecrated bishop in 1831 but accusations of sexual misconduct resulted in his suspension in the 1840s.  Disputes raged over the justice of this between the tractarian and evangelical wings of the American episcopal church until his death.  It was not he, but the Bishop of western New York, the Rt. Rev. William Heathcote DeLancey, whom CMY met at the SPG meeting in Winchester in 1852.

It was certainly he, and not the Bishop of New York at this period, the Rt. Rev. Benjamin Treadwell Onderdonk, who attended the anniversary meeting of the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel as representative of the American Episcopal Church.

The Collins family seem to have consisted of Martha (Andrews) Collins (b. 1805/6), postmistress, wife of George Collins, (b. 1818/9) of the Post Office, Otterbourne, groom and gardener, and their children George (b. 1839/40),  Charles (b.1840/1), Elizabeth (b. 1844/5),  and Anne (b. 1846/7).

Two portraits by Richmond of CMY exist, one in the NPG, the other a sketch of her head. He also painted WCY (the picture reproduced in Coleridge Life), Keble (at the behest of Sir William Heathcote) and Mary Ann Moberly. In Richmond\'s archive in the Royal Academy are some letters about the Keble commission, including one from Heathcote telling Richmond to ignore WCY\'s attempts to interfere with the design.
He was buried in the nave of Canterbury Cathedral on 26 February 1853.

biography: Harriet Harvey (Holbeton 1800/1-1854) is recorded in the 1841 census as a female servant at Puslinch, and in the 1851 census as a schoolmistress, living alone in the village of Torre in Newton Ferrars parish.
An inhabitant of Newton Ferrars, perhaps a relation of Harriet Harvey.

She was the mother of the 5th Earl of Rosebery (1847-1929), the Prime Minister, who was at this date a child and the holder of the courtesy title Lord Dalmeny.
